About us

A pain centre built around one question: where is this actually coming from?

Halcyon relieves pain with advanced non-surgical treatment, using the latest interventional techniques at an affordable cost — so that people can get back to living pain-free lives.

Why Halcyon
10+ Years in Pain Medicine US FDA-Cleared COOLIEF Cooled RF CIPS — World Institute of Pain, USA Ultrasound-Guided Precision Day-Care Procedures No General Anaesthesia 10+ Years in Pain Medicine US FDA-Cleared COOLIEF Cooled RF CIPS — World Institute of Pain, USA Ultrasound-Guided Precision Day-Care Procedures No General Anaesthesia

A comprehensive pain management centre in Kukatpally, Hyderabad.

Halcyon treats long-standing pain the way it behaves — as something with a source that has to be found before it can be treated. Pain that lasts is rarely where it hurts, so every appointment begins with an examination and a diagnostic ultrasound, and the treatment follows from what those show.

Nothing here needs a scalpel. Procedures are image-guided, done under local anaesthetic while you are awake, and you go home the same day.

Diagnosis and treatment in the same appointment.

The consultant who takes your history is the one who scans you, reads the scan and — when it says a procedure is the right answer — performs it before you leave. Nothing is handed to a second team, and nothing has to be explained twice.

Appointments are spaced through the day, so the wait is short. Most people are home inside two hours of arriving.

See the visit in full
  1. 0:00You arrive

    Reception takes your details and any scans or reports you have brought with you.

  2. 0:15You meet the consultant

    History and examination, working out which structure is generating the pain.

  3. 0:35Diagnostic ultrasound

    The suspected joint, tendon or nerve is scanned in the same room.

  4. 1:05The scan sets the treatment

    If an image-guided procedure is right, it is done there and then under local anaesthetic.

  5. 1:45You go home

    No admission and no general anaesthetic — with aftercare instructions and a review date.
